name: Pinkish red
lede: Pinkish red is the dictionary's all-purpose gloss for a red with a pink cast, used to define lobster, rose, ruby and brick before it was ever a color name of its own.

sections.title: A gloss, not a name
sections.body: Paterson uses the phrase to define a long list of colors: adobe, after the sun-dried bricks of Latin America [1]; the Burmese ruby [2]; the homard, or lobster [3]; permanent rose, pink carmine and the red of the rose itself [4]. Pomegranate is sometimes called pinkish red too, though its rind is golden-orange to red [5]. The web color `LightCoral`, #F08080, gets the same gloss [6]. See [[crimson]], [[rose]], [[adobe]] and [[coral]] for named relatives.

sections.title: Incarnadine and the earths
sections.body: St Clair's glossary defines incarnadine as a fierce, saturated pinkish red [7]. For earth pigments, Church in 1901 wrote that the terra rosa of Italy owes its pinkish-red hue to ferric oxide [8]. A synthetic dye shows up as well: erythrosine, a pinkish-red stain, is the food additive E127 used in glacé cherries [9].

sections.title: The color of a low sun
sections.body: Pastoureau notes that sunlight reads yellow or yellow-orange at midday, but yellowish red, pinkish red or even red when the sun is rising or setting [10]. He adds that these are modern scientific explanations unknown to ancient societies [10].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch here is the xkcd survey's Pinkish Red, #F10C45, a vivid, saturated color [11]. Its nearest named color is Crimson, at a color distance (ΔE) of 4.4, and the Wikipedia color list has a near-duplicate called Red (Munsell) at 2.1 [11]. No painting in the ColorHub archive of 23,531 carries it as photographed [12].
